findings.title: NameError: PRCommentWorkflow is not defined in CommitContextIntegration scope
findings.body: In `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`, the code calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but `PRCommentWorkflow` is not imported or defined in this file. The `_truncate_title` static method is defined on `CommitContextIntegration` itself. This will raise a `NameError` at runtime whenever a merged PR comment is generated (called from both GitHub and GitLab integration `get_comment_body`). The fix is to use `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(title)` or simply `_truncate_title(title)` since it's a static method on the same class.

findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) may pair wrong event IDs with wrong data
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict that may omit missing keys and does not guarantee ordering matches the input list. Using `zip(error_ids, events.values())` will silently pair the wrong event_id with the wrong event data when any node is missing from the result. For example, if error_ids=['a','b','c'] but only nodes for 'a' and 'c' are found, 'a' gets paired with 'a's data correctly only by coincidence; 'b' would be paired with 'c's data. The correct approach is to iterate over `error_ids` and look up each corresponding node_id in the returned dict.

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty data when feature flag is enabled
findings.body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the component renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` with completely empty columns and data. The actual table results available in `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, etc. from the surrounding `tableResults.map` iteration are never passed. Users with this feature flag enabled will see an empty table instead of their dashboard widget data.

findings.title: Mutual exclusion validation uses truthiness check, allowing age=0 with timestamp present
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` checks `self.initial_data.get('age')` which is a truthiness test. If a report contains both `timestamp` and `age=0`, the check evaluates to falsy and no validation error is raised, violating the spec constraint that these fields are mutually exclusive. The same issue exists in `validate_age` with `self.initial_data.get('timestamp')` if timestamp were 0 (though min_value=0 makes 0 valid). Use `'age' in self.initial_data` instead of truthiness to correctly detect field presence.

findings.title: Migration test removed without replacement for the corrected migration
findings.body: The test for migration 0917 is deleted, and migrations 0917 and 0920 are gutted to no-ops referencing `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py` as the correct migration. However, migration 0921 and its test are not included in this PR. If the replacement migration is landed separately, there's a window where the data conversion has no test coverage, and if it's not landed, the conversion silently never happens for environments that haven't yet applied 0917/0920.

findings.title: get_request_data mutates the input error_events list via in-place sort
findings.body: `error_events.sort(key=lambda x: x['timestamp'])` sorts the list in place. The `error_events` list is constructed in the endpoint's `get` method and passed via `functools.partial` to `analyze_recording_segments`. While currently safe because the list is only used once, in-place mutation of a caller-owned list is fragile and can cause subtle bugs if the list is reused or if the function is called multiple times with the same list.
